exposure: Delivery mode (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery for abnormal second stage of labor, cesarean delivery for other indications)
outcome: Pelvic floor disorders (PFDs) and related repair diagnoses
cohort: 106,003 women who delivered between 1991-2017 at a tertiary medical center
finding: Cesarean delivery was found to be protective against later PFD development only if performed before the second stage of labor, suggesting that the protective effect of cesarean delivery on PFDs might be related to avoiding the second stage of labor rather than cesarean delivery itself.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery may be protective against later PFD development only if performed prior to the second stage of labor.
